newsitem.title: USA: USDA's Glickman reviewing EU modified-gene labels.
newsitem.headline: USDA's Glickman reviewing EU modified-gene labels.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said the U.S. is reviewing a European Union decision Wednesday to require labelling of genetically-modified farm products as of July 31 to gauge the affects on trade.
"We need to look closely at the change to determine if it will disrupt trade, that is something that obviously worries us," Glickman told reporters after speaking to a dairy group.
"I remain very suspicious of most of the labelling schemes that I have seen in this area, but I'd like to reserve comment until I've seen exactly what they've done," he said.
Earlier, the European Commission formally approved new rules that require labels specify a product "may contain or may consist of genetically modified organisms" (GMOs).
Glickman said if the EU move hampered trade, USDA would consult with the U.S. Trade Representative's Office to see if there were remedies under various trade laws.
But he added, "I don't want to send a shot across the bow until I actually see what they have done."
Glickman said he would reinforce the U.S. position that "good science" prevail on biotechnology issues with EU agriculture ministers at an International Grains Council meeting in London on Thursday.
